newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel confident of support for safety review.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel confident of support for safety review.

text.p: Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel Plc said on Thursday it was confident its revised safety procedures, unveiled earlier, would be cleared by the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority (CTSA).

Patrick Ponsolle, co-chairman, told a press conference, "We've spent the last few weeks discussing proposals in depth (with the CTSA) and these are still going on and will continue into the coming weeks."
"The progress we've made is enough for us to predict that we will be allowed resumption of (HGV) services in mid-June."
Ponsolle said the start-date of HGV (heavy goods vehicle) freight services had been pushed back to June from May to allow for time to implement the new safety procedures.
Eurotunnel unveiled its new safety procedures after announcing the results of its internal inquiry into the tunnel fire last November.
That major fire damaged a section of the tunnel and led to suspension of some services.
But the final judgement on when Eurotunnel is allowed to resume normal freight services will come from the CTSA and the governments of France and Britain.

Fellow Eurotunnel chairman, Robert Malpas also denied claims from the Kent Fire Brigade in England and press reports that the open-sided design of the freight wagons created a "blow-torch" effect on the night of last year's fire.
He said there was no evidence to support this view and that Eurotunnel had therefore decided against redesigning the wagons.
"I've read reports of the blow torch effect and I'm telling you, it does not exist. It is a fantasy."
